name: Night Web's Hollow
summary: Northwest of Deathknell, spiders infest a gold mine the Forsaken need. Executor Arren sends newly risen recruits into the cavern to cull the spiders piece by piece. Raw materials are scarce, and the mine's wealth could sustain the Forsaken settlement and war effort.

sections.title: A Nation in Need of Coin
sections.body: Executor Arren oversees operations in Deathknell, where the newly risen Forsaken struggle to survive. They face the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, but defending themselves is only part of the work. A fledgling society also needs raw materials. Precious metals such as gold were scarce in northern Lordaeron even when the Alliance was strong. Arren knows the Forsaken need wealth to arm and equip themselves and establish their society.

sections.title: The Infested Mine
sections.body: A natural cavern called Night Web's Hollow lies northwest of Deathknell's cemetery, with a gold vein running through it. Monstrous spiders have overrun its tunnels, leaving thick webs and deadly venom in their depths. Arren has too few seasoned troops for a full purge, so fresh recruits thin the young and adult spiders. Once the danger is reduced, mining crews can burn away the webs and extract the ore.

faq.q: Why do the undead need a gold mine?
faq.answer: The Forsaken need gold to fund their war effort, buy supplies, and rebuild settlements across Tirisfal Glades. Lordaeron has always lacked natural resources, and a new realm independent of both the Alliance and the Scourge needs valuable currency to trade and procure equipment.

Executor Arren is Deathknell's ranking military authority. He organizes the newly risen undead and secures the immediate perimeter, directing recruits to hunt Scourge remnants, gather supplies, and open local resources.

faq.q: Where is Night Web's Hollow located?
faq.answer: Night Web's Hollow lies northwest of Deathknell's main settlement and graveyard, among rocky bluffs in a secluded valley in Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: Are the Forsaken able to mine the gold immediately after this quest?
faq.answer: Not right away. Arren says eradicating the spiders will take weeks or months of sustained effort. Then crews must use torches to burn away the pervasive webs before miners can safely excavate the veins.

faq.q: Why doesn't Arren send a full detachment of soldiers to clear the cave?
faq.answer: Deathknell's garrison is stretched thin guarding against mindless Scourge prowling the outskirts and watching for Scarlet Crusade scouts. Arren lacks spare manpower to assign a regular squad to pest control, so newly risen recruits clear the mine bit by bit.

faq.q: Can spider venom harm the undead?
faq.answer: Caustic spider venom can burn preserved flesh and weaken reanimated limbs, even though the Forsaken do not bleed or breathe like the living. Arren warns recruits to watch for a sharp burning sensation and seek treatment if afflicted.

angles.text: As an Undead, you face a harsh reality in reclaimed Lordaeron: survival means securing ordinary needs like metal and coin, not just seeking vengeance against the living and the Scourge.
As a miner, you know thick webs and predatory spiders make prospecting perilous in this cavern, one of Deathknell's few nearby sources of gold ore.
As a member of the Horde, you know secured resources in Tirisfal Glades help establish the Forsaken as a reliable northern stronghold.
